playbooks.title: Injury on site

steps.do: Tap stop on every device near the incident. Nobody films an injury.
Help the person. Call the site medical staff. If it is serious, call an ambulance. Do not wait for permission.
Call the Portfolio Manager. Tell them where you are, what happened, who is hurt, how the person is, and whether an ambulance was called.
Go to the site. Stay with the person until the medical staff take over. Keep everyone on the site calm.
Call Moharam and Adham. Tell them what happened and how the person is. Moharam talks to the site owner.

Make the place safe before anyone films there again. Check the PPE, the cables, and the tethers on any work done above the ground. If the site's setup caused the injury, nobody films there until it is fixed.

Write down what happened, who saw it, and what changed. Do this while you still remember it well. Put it in the wrap report tonight. If a phone fell from a high place, write that as a separate incident in the report.

tell.by: Now, from the operator
Now, from the operator
Within 30 minutes, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, in the wrap report. Mano does the paperwork and any insurance claim

playbooks.never: Never keep recording. An injury comes before every rule, including the cycle.

playbooks.title: Theft or vehicle loss
playbooks.first: Get yourself to a safe place. Then call Moharam.

steps.do: Get yourself to a safe place. If anyone is hurt, follow the injury playbook first. Then call Moharam. Tell him where you are, what happened, and the device count on the manifest.
Find every device on the manifest in MDM. Location tracking was turned on for the trip. Use it.
Put every device on the manifest in lost mode. A locked phone has no value to the person who has it.
File the police report. The runner goes to the police station with the manifest and the copy of the commercial register.
Open the insurance claim. Attach the police report, the manifest, and the registry rows. Mark each registry row as lost.
Send replacement phones to the site from the 10% spare pool. Then the site can film tomorrow with its full number of phones.
Wipe every device that has not been found. Close the registry row for each one.

Review the run. Did the run carry a third of the site's phones or less? Was the case locked and unmarked? Was custody signed? Was the run before 11 PM? Any deduction follows the handbook, and only after this review.

tell.by: Now, from the runner
Same hour, from Moharam, for the claim and the replacements
Same hour, so the site knows which phones are coming back and when
Same day, from Moharam

playbooks.never: Never wipe a phone first. First find it, then lock it, then wait 24 hours, then wipe it. A wiped phone cannot be found.

playbooks.title: Police checkpoint
playbooks.first: Pull over and stay calm. Let the letter answer the officer's questions.

steps.do: Hand over the Arabic company letter, the copy of the commercial register, and the manifest. These are the papers the officer is asking for.

Explain what you carry in plain words. Say that these are company phones, and that they are going between a company site and the company's upload facility. Give the exact count. Point to the two numbers on the letter.
Call Moharam from the checkpoint. Tell him where you are, who is asking, and what they want.

Answer the officer's call. Confirm who the runner is, what the company is, and what the count is. If the officer asks what the work is, say it is video for a robotics research program. Say nothing more.
If the police keep the devices, get a written receipt. The receipt must show the count, who holds the devices, and where they are held. Do not drive away without it.
Go with the lawyer and the company documents. Get the held devices released.
Count every device that comes back. Check the count against the manifest. Log the custody event. The registry, MDM, and the phones in your hand must all show the same count.
Log the checkpoint. Write where it was, when it was, what the police asked, and what the runner showed. The runners who drive on that road tomorrow need to know this.

tell.by: Now, from the checkpoint
Same hour, if the police keep any device or paper
Same hour, if the phones will be late, so the site can plan without them
Same day, from Mano, if the police keep any devices

playbooks.never: Never argue, and never hide the count. Let the letter and the manifest answer the questions.

playbooks.title: Uploads stop at a hub
playbooks.first: Send tonight's runs to the second hub.

steps.do: Check that the problem is the internet line. Turn the router and the switch off and on again, one time. If the uploads do not start again, call Mano.
Open a ticket with the ISP. Get a ticket number and the time they promise to fix it.
Send every run that has not been delivered yet to the second hub. Tell each runner before the runner leaves the site. Runs still end at 11 PM.

Move the phones that are waiting at the hub that is down to the second hub. Use the same runs. Write a new manifest for each case. Phones that already show zero pending uploads go back to their sites as normal.
Count the backlog for each site in device-days. Put it in the wrap report. If any site has more than one device-day of backlog, write it up as a separate incident.
In the morning, before any phone leaves the second hub, check on the dashboard that all of its uploads finished. A phone leaves only when it is empty. If it is not empty, it does not leave.
If the line is still down after 24 hours, open the tested day-pass location and send the extra phones there. When the ISP closes the ticket, test the line before the next run arrives at the hub.

tell.by: Now, from the hub attendant
Same hour, from Mano. Moharam is responsible for the result.

tell.who: Every Portfolio Manager with a hub site
tell.by: Same hour, so their runners know where to drive
Same day, in the executive sync. If the line is down for more than 24 hours, tell him the same hour.

playbooks.never: Never upload from someone's home to get around the problem. Use a tested hub or a day-pass location. Use nothing else.

playbooks.title: Power cut
playbooks.first: Plug the router into the UPS. Keep the cycles running.

steps.do: Check that the router and the switch are plugged into the UPS and their lights are on. If they are not, move them to the UPS now.
steps.owner: Operator at a site, hub attendant at a hub

steps.do: Keep the cycles running. The phones record on their batteries. If the site itself stops work, tap stop. Footage of people who are not working is fraud.
Tell the Portfolio Manager which site it is, when the power went off, how long the site expects the cut to last, and how many phones have a low battery.
Swap the phones with a low battery for charged spares. When the power comes back, empty any phone with a storage warning first.
At a hub, the uploads keep going on battery power. If the power is still off when the runs are due, Moharam sends the runs to the second hub.

The UPS can power a router for hours, not days. If the power is still off when the UPS runs out, the site becomes a hub site for tonight. That means a third of the phones go in each run, custody is signed, and the runs finish before 11 PM.
At the end of the shift, count the backlog in device-days. Put it in the wrap report. If any site has more than one device-day of backlog, write it up as a separate incident.
Recharge or replace the UPS before you need it again. If the UPS ran empty tonight, it will still be empty on Thursday night.
steps.owner: Portfolio Manager, with Mano for a replacement

tell.by: Same hour, from the operator
Same hour, if the runs must go to the second hub or the UPS will not last the shift
Same day, for a replacement UPS or a hub question
Same day, in the executive sync, if hours were lost

playbooks.never: Never let a full phone sit overnight because the power went off. The runner and the hub exist for exactly this kind of night.

playbooks.title: Many accounts banned at once
playbooks.first: Stop all filming on the banned accounts. Tell QC and Moharam within the hour.

steps.do: Take the wearer off the work and have them sit down. Nobody films on a banned account. Nobody logs in on another person's account.
Tell Youssef Medhat and Moharam which site it is, which accounts were banned, and which sessions were affected.

Open the sessions that caused each ban. Find the pattern. The pattern is one of these: the wearer was idle, the hat was off while recording, the camera pointed at the torso or the floor, the tasks were staged, the wearer recorded the screen, or the wearer filmed someone else. Use the wearer log to match each session to a wearer.
Walk around the site. Check the angle of every rig, check every hat, and check that every wearer is on their own account. Fix the problem the pattern shows. Retrain the wearers right there.
Look for the same pattern on every other site. If you find it, every Portfolio Manager fixes it today.
Remove any wearer who was banned for fraud. They do not come back, not under any name and not on any device. Deductions follow the handbook.
Only new people get new accounts, and only through onboarding screening. A banned account is never used again.

tell.by: Same hour, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, from Youssef Medhat
Same day, from Moharam, with the pattern and the fix. Adham handles anything the client says about it.
Same day, for the wearer log, the removals, and any new accounts through the gate

playbooks.never: Never bring back a worker who was removed. Never use an old account again. This is true even with a new name or a new device.

playbooks.title: A worker who may be a minor
playbooks.first: Do not put a device on them, not even for one cycle.

steps.do: Do not give them a device. If they are already wearing one, tap stop and take it off them now.
Tell the Portfolio Manager which site it is, who assigned the person, and whether any footage was recorded.
Check the wearer log and the ID on file. The ID number shows the birth date. If there is no ID on file, the person never passed the gate.
If any footage was recorded, take the device out of use. Send the device number, the account, and the shift times to Youssef Medhat.
Find every session from that wearer. Delete each one before it reaches the client. When this is done, tell the Portfolio Manager and Mano.

Tell Mano which site it is, who assigned the person, which device, which account, and whether footage was recorded. If the site made us take this person, tell Moharam too. Moharam talks to the site about it.
Check the gate again for every wearer on that site. Each wearer must have an ID on file, a signed consent, and a row in the wearer log. If one person got through without these, others may have too.

tell.by: Now, from the operator
Same hour, if any footage was recorded
Same day, always. Mano runs the gate.
Same day, if the site made us take the person
Same day, from Mano, if any footage reached the client

playbooks.never: Never trust what a site tells you about someone's age. Nobody films without an ID on file, no matter who assigned them.

playbooks.title: A client complaint
playbooks.first: Say nothing to the client. Send the complaint to Moharam now.

steps.do: Do not reply. Send the complaint to Moharam exactly as you received it. Tell him who sent it, what it says, and how it reached you.
Take over the conversation with the client. Ask the client for the session IDs, the accounts, and the dates, so the search is exact.
Find the sessions. For each one, find the site, the device, the wearer through the wearer log, and what our review said at the time. Say clearly whether we missed the problem.
Check whether the same problem is happening on any other site. If it is, every Portfolio Manager fixes it today.

Fix the problem on the site. Retrain the wearer, fix the rig, change the rotation, or remove the worker if this is their third flag. Do this within 24 hours of the complaint. Do not wait for the next sync.
Report back to Adham. Tell him which sessions were found, what the cause was, what changed, and what was deleted.
Close the complaint with the client. Send one reply. Say what happened and what changed. Report the follow-up work in the Sunday update.

tell.by: Now, from the person who received it
Same hour, from Moharam. Adham writes every word that goes to the client.
Same hour, to find the sessions
Same day, with the sessions and the fix
Same day, if it is about the collection app, exports, or data handling

playbooks.never: Never contact the client. Do not contact them to say sorry, to explain, or to ask a question. Only Adham talks to the client.

playbooks.title: A disagreement with a partner
playbooks.first: Do not promise anything right away. Call Moharam.

steps.do: Listen. Write down who raised the problem, what they said, and whether filming is paused. Do not promise anything.
Call Moharam and read him the note. A partner complaint does not wait for the daily sync.
Take over the relationship with the partner. Talk to the partner. Settle the operational matters. These are access, shifts, staff, and phones.
Take over the money side. Questions about payment, hours, and fees go to Mano and nobody else. Everyone is paid on accepted hours, minus the hours with fraud flags. That rule does not change.
Count the partner's devices in MDM today and check the count against the registry. No payment goes out until the count matches.
If the problem is about the terms of the agreement or about ending it, bring in Adham. The founders settle it. Moharam and Mano do not renegotiate the terms.

If the partnership ends, start the exit today. Set a return date no later than 7 days from now. Count every device back against the registry and MDM, and tick the condition of each one. MDM gives us control. Put any device that is not back on day 7 in lost mode. Make the final payment only after the count matches.
Protect the hours. If filming is paused, move the phones and the people to a site where they can record hours. Write this in the wrap report.

tell.by: Now, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, for anything about money or devices
Same day, from Moharam. Adham owns the contract. He decides whether the founders get involved.
Same day, to do the count

playbooks.never: Never send a payment while the device count is not finished. The agreement says this, and it is there for exactly this situation.
